# Results — Study 591 (Vol-Managed Portfolio)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test
(Moreira & Muir 2017, JF) — **scaling equity exposure by inverse realized variance raises the
Sharpe ratio and earns alpha over buy-and-hold, because volatility is forecastable while the
equity premium is not** — rebuilt on SPY (headline) with QQQ / EFA / IWM robustness legs.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped).
Fingerprint `11ef90f96ced`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **total-return** (auto-adjusted) closes: SPY 1993-02→2026-06, QQQ 1999+, EFA 2001+, IWM 2000+; risk-free = **^IRX** 13-week T-bill (`IRX/100/252` per day) |
| Window (SPY) | 1993-02-01 → 2026-06-30 (**8,410** days, **401** complete months; **388** strategy months after the 12-month RV burn-in) |
| The rule | at month-*m* close: `w(m+1) = min(1.5, c_m / RV_m)` with `RV_m` = sum of squared daily returns of month *m* and `c_m` = **expanding** (past-only) mean of monthly RV — **no full-sample look-ahead** in the normaliser, unlike the paper's ex-post variance-matching constant |
| Execution lag | **exactly one**: the signal uses only month-*m* daily returns, all known at the month-*m* close where the month-*m+1* weight is set. No same-bar information |
| Race convention | **excess-vs-excess** everywhere: both legs subtract the same T-bill rate; leverage above 1 is financed at that rate inside `w × excess`, and the retail **borrow spread** on `max(w−1,0)` is charged separately in the cost sweep |
| Costs | one-way bps × \|Δw\| × NAV per monthly rebalance (avg \|Δw\| = **0.210**/mo) + 1–2%/yr borrow spread on the levered fraction |
| Survivorship | none at the instrument level — single continuously-listed broad-index ETFs, no basket selection |

Average weight **1.12**; the 1.5× cap binds in **48.7%** of months.

## The race — managed vs buy-and-hold (SPY, gross, excess-vs-excess)

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| Sharpe (ann), managed | **0.717** |
| Sharpe (ann), buy-and-hold | 0.606 |
| **HAC alpha** (managed on unmanaged) | **+2.87%/yr** · NW *t* = **+2.004** (Bartlett, 5 lags) |
| beta | 0.844 |
| appraisal ratio | **0.383** (residual vol 7.5%/yr) |

The Moreira-Muir alpha on SPY clears the desk bar **at the wire**: NW *t* = **2.004** on
388 months, gross. The Sharpe rises from 0.606 to 0.717 with a beta of 0.84 — the strategy
de-levers into storms and re-levers in calm, exactly the paper's mechanism.

## Placebo — shuffle the vol signal (200 seeds, full rule rebuilt per seed)

Permuting the monthly RV series across months (same marginal distribution, no timing
information) kills the alpha:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed alpha | **+2.87%/yr** (*t* = +2.00) |
| shuffled alpha, mean over 200 seeds | +0.01%/yr · mean *t* = **−0.06** (sd 1.12) |
| **p[shuffled ≥ observed]** | **0.030** |

The alpha lives in the *alignment* of the RV signal with the months that follow it — a random
same-distribution vol signal earns nothing (mean *t* ≈ 0), and only 3.0% of shuffles beat the tape.

## Net of costs — the certified edge dies at retail frictions

| scenario | alpha (%/yr) | NW *t* | Sharpe managed vs B&H |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| gross | **+2.87** | **+2.00** | 0.717 vs 0.606 |
| 5 bps one-way + 1%/yr borrow spread | +2.46 | **+1.72** | 0.690 vs 0.606 |
| 10 bps one-way + 2%/yr borrow spread | +2.06 | +1.44 | 0.662 vs 0.606 |

Trading costs are almost irrelevant (turnover is tiny at 0.21 |Δw|/month); the **borrow spread
on the levered half of the calendar** is what bites. Net of a realistic retail margin spread the
point estimate stays positive (+2.5%/yr) and the Sharpe still beats buy-and-hold, but the
alpha is **no longer certified** (*t* = 1.72 < 2).

## Robustness — other assets, and the cap

| leg | months | alpha (%/yr) | NW *t* | Sharpe managed vs B&H |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **SPY (headline)** | 388 | **+2.87** | **+2.00** | 0.717 vs 0.606 |
| QQQ | 315 | **+5.49** | **+2.61** | 0.556 vs 0.383 |
| EFA | 285 | +1.92 | +0.84 | 0.507 vs 0.456 |
| IWM | 300 | +1.71 | +0.72 | 0.470 vs 0.437 |

| cap | alpha (%/yr) | NW *t* | Sharpe managed vs B&H |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1.0× (long-only, de-lever only) | +1.44 | +1.44 | 0.676 vs 0.606 |
| **1.5× (headline)** | **+2.87** | **+2.00** | 0.717 vs 0.606 |
| 2.0× | +3.99 | +2.17 | 0.728 vs 0.606 |

The verdict **splits by leg**: US large-cap and especially Nasdaq clear the bar
(*t* = 2.00 / 2.61); international developed and US small-cap do not (*t* = 0.7–0.8) — the
alpha point estimates stay positive everywhere but only the US-megacap legs certify. It also
needs the leverage: the long-only 1.0× version (all Sharpe-improvement, half the alpha) sits at
*t* = 1.44, and the alpha grows with the cap.

## Third axis — does it dodge crashes? (max drawdown, monthly total-return NAVs)

| window | managed | buy-and-hold |
|---|--:|--:|
| GFC 2008-09 | **−31.0%** | −50.8% |
| COVID 2020 | −18.2% | −19.4% |
| 2022 bear | **−15.8%** | −20.2% |
| full sample | **−39.4%** | −50.8% |

**Mixed, and exactly as the mechanism predicts.** The monthly RV signal dodges *slow-burn*
crashes — vol was already elevated for months before Lehman, so the strategy entered 2008-09 at
low weight and cut the GFC drawdown by ~20 points (−31% vs −51%). It **cannot** dodge *sudden*
crashes: February 2020 followed one of the calmest Januaries on record, the strategy was levered
≈1.5× going in, and the COVID drawdown matched buy-and-hold (−18.2% vs −19.4%). The 2022
grind (vol rising all year) was again partially dodged.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful (never cited for the stamp)

Deterministic 30-year daily worlds with persistent log-vol AR(1) clustering, 20 seeds averaged;
the ``disconnect`` knob sets how conditional mean relates to conditional variance
(unconditional mean identical in every world):

| world | mean HAC alpha *t* (20 seeds) | mean alpha (%/yr) | share of seeds *t* ≥ 2 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **NULL** — mean ∝ variance (risk fully priced) | **−0.08** (sd 1.24) | −0.10 | 0% |
| flat mean while vol swings | +1.08 (sd 1.10) | +2.44 | 25% |
| **PLANTED leverage effect** — mean falls as variance rises | **+2.09** (sd 0.98) | +5.01 | 60% |

The overlay earns **nothing** in the fully-priced null however the noise falls, and **banks the
planted leverage-effect world** (mean *t* = 2.09). The flat-mean row is a power lesson: even in
a *true* mild Moreira-Muir world, 30 years of monthly data often can't certify the alpha —
context for why the real-tape *t* sits near 2. *(Machinery proof only — never market evidence.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** On the real tape the Moreira-Muir alpha clears the bar on the US
  mega-cap legs — SPY **+2.87%/yr at NW *t* = 2.00** (at the wire), QQQ **+5.49%/yr at
  *t* = 2.61**, shuffled-signal placebo **p = 0.030** — but **fails on EFA (+0.84) and IWM
  (+0.72)**, and the long-only 1.0× variant sits at *t* = 1.44. Real on US large/growth,
  unsupported elsewhere: **Mixed**, per the desk's split-by-leg rule. No survivorship (single
  continuously-listed index ETFs).
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** Turnover is negligible, capacity is effectively unlimited (SPY),
  and the vehicle is retail-accessible — but the strategy *needs the 1.5× leverage half* of the
  calendar, and once a realistic retail margin spread is charged the alpha decertifies
  (**+2.46%/yr, *t* = 1.72** at 5 bps + 1% spread; *t* = 1.44 at 10 bps + 2%). A real
  Sharpe improvement you can hold, whose *certified* alpha does not survive retail frictions.
- **Does it dodge crashes? — MIXED.** It dodged the slow-burn crashes (GFC **−31% vs −51%**,
  2022 **−16% vs −20%**) and completely missed the sudden one (COVID **−18.2% vs −19.4%**,
  entered levered off a calm January). Vol-managing is crash *insurance only against storms
  that announce themselves*.
